correctness.rationale: PASS: For prescribed output (s,Q) on (0,1)xR and 0<k<1, invert the affine belief update q=(Q-kp0-kp1 x)/(1-k); substituting into the logistic coordinate gives the equivalent scalar equation H(x)=L(s,Q), H=logit(x)-a beta x, beta=[1-k(1+cp1)]/(1-k). H tends to -infinity/+infinity at endpoints, giving surjectivity. H'(x)=1/[x(1-x)]-a beta, and det DF=(1-k)s(1-s)H'(x): beta<=0 or a beta<4 gives a smooth positive-orientation global inverse. At a beta=4, H increases strictly but derivative vanishes at x=1/2 and local Taylor coefficient 16/3 yields cubic inverse singularity. Above 4, two fold abscissae (1±sqrt(1-4/Lambda))/2 divide three monotonic intervals and yield exactly one, two or three inverse points depending on target level. The width W=Lambda*d-4atanh(d)~(Lambda-4)^(3/2)/3; at k=1 the inverse is separately smooth onto Q in (p0,p0+p1). The explicit a=6log3, c=500, k=2/5, p1=1/1000 three physical input witness has identical exact output and Jacobian signs +,-,+; independently recalculated q outputs, logits and signs. No claim that every supercritical parameter has a three-point physical fiber.
